thread:
maria: Found an embedded Vault token in a terraform state file in CI artifacts S3. s3://redwood-ci-artifacts/tfstates/provision/2026-03-18.tfstate.gz. Token scopes look like staging/* — can we rotate and revoke ASAP? tagging @jake @priya @laura-security

jake: on it. can you paste the snippet? redact actual token pls

maria: redacted snippet:
```
"vault_generic_secret": {
  "data": {
    "vault_token": "s.REDACTEDabcd1234"
  }
}
```
I ran `jq` locally. Found in object `module.db.aws_s3_bucket_object.tfstate`

priya: If token is still active, we should revoke it and rotate the underlying SA/KMS wrapping. Quick mitigation steps: 
1) revoke token: `vault token revoke <token>`
2) search for other tfstate files: `aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-ci-artifacts --prefix tfstates/provision --query 'Contents[].Key'`
3) if KMS-wrapped, rewrap secrets with new key versions. We'll need to coordinate with Infra.

alok: I'll start the s3/repo sweep and open a Jira. Sam, can you handle KMS/key rotation? @oncall-bot please run secret-scan playbook.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-78 'tfstate embedded vault token' assigned to eng-security. Playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/secrets-incident

sam: Happy to rotate. Quick Q: Are these tokens long-lived or CI short-lived service tokens? If CI, rotate by re-running pipelines with updated secrets. If SA keys, I'll create a new key, update the secrets engine to use the new wrapping key, then destroy old key versions.

laura-security: We need audit logs for token use before revoke. Priya, can you pull Vault audit logs for the last 48h? If audit isn't enabled for that mount, enable file audit temporarily: `vault audit enable file file_path=/var/log/vault_audit_incident.log`

priya: Pulling logs now. initial check: token was used to read `secret/staging/db-creds` at 2026-03-18T14:02Z from IP 35.196.10.44. No writes. I'll paste a short summary in a sec.

maria: mitigation update: copied the tfstate locally and moved the original to s3://redwood-security-evidence/INC-2026-78/provision-2026-03-18.tfstate.gz (private). Removed public ACL and replaced the object with an empty placeholder.

jake: once logs are captured, rotate token and revoke. also run a grep across repos and CI artifacts for `vault_token` or `terraform.tfstate` leaks: `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 grep -n "vault_token\|terraform.tfstate"` and `aws s3api list-objects ...`

alok: Sweep started. Found 6 tfstate objects in the provision bucket with possible embedded secrets. Listing keys and tagging them for rotation now.

sam: I'll schedule a 15-min rotation window at 2026-03-18T15:20Z UTC. Plan:
``
1. create new KMS key version (if applicable)
2. rewrap secrets: `aws kms re-encrypt` or `gcloud kms encrypt` depending on cloud
3. update CI vars to new wrapped values
4. re-run CI to refresh tokens/creds
5. revoke old tokens/keys
```
I'll post status updates here.

priya: Audit summary: token read only; used by CI runner `ci-runner-7`. IP resolves to our GCP project. Looks like terraform pushed the state with token embedded during the CI step. No external IPs. Still recommend rotation and hardening.

laura-security: RBAC change proposal: require that tokens created by pipelines are constrained to `ci/*` paths with explicit policies and TTL <= 1h. Add policy enforcement in infra templates and require auditors to signoff on any pipeline changes that create tokens. Also increase Vault audit log retention to 90 days for critical mounts. I'll open PRs for infra-ops and ci-config.

maria: FYI I've removed the original tfstate from public bucket and replaced with an empty placeholder file. Evidence copy lives in redwood-security-evidence bucket with restricted ACLs.

oncall-bot: INC-2026-78 status: investigation -> mitigation in progress -> assigned to sam, alok, priya

jake: :thumbsup: keep updates here. After rotation we'll run a secondary review of the CI artifacts push flow and consider adding server-side checks to prevent tokens in tfstate.

sam: Rotation in progress — created new KMS key version and rewrapped secrets, updated CI variables, re-ran pipelines to refresh tokens. Revoking old token now:`vault token revoke s.REDACTEDabcd1234` and `vault token revoke <other-old-tokens>`

priya: Confirming from Vault audit: last use of old token at 2026-03-18T15:18Z, revocation recorded at 2026-03-18T15:21Z. No further reads detected. S3 objects flagged as cleaned/rotated.

laura-security: Thanks all — please follow up with a short postmortem and RBAC policy PR. Assigning to @maria to draft the postmortem and @alok to attach list of affected artifacts and keys.

maria: Drafting postmortem now, will post to #postmortems when ready.

jake: Also scheduling an automated sweep job next week to search for tfstate files with embedded secrets and to add a CI lint that blocks pushes with tokens.

sam: Rotation complete and old keys/tokens revoked. Closing incident — reopen if additional findings are discovered.

maria: thanks everyone, layered fixes look good.
